devices.definition: A word or words deliberately left out, to be supplied by the reader — compression and force.

devices.name: Metonymy
devices.definition: Naming something by a word closely associated with it — cause for effect, container for contents, author for writings.

occurrences.note: " What have I sinned, that thou wouldest deliver thy servant (i.e., cause to be delivered) into the hand of Ahab to slay me ? "
" Yet I have left me seven thousand in Israel, all the knees which have not bowed unto Baal, and every mouth which hath not kissed him ": i.e., have not obeyed or worshipped him

devices.name: Synecdoche
devices.definition: Substituting a part for the whole, or the whole for a part (“all the world”; “flesh and blood”).

occurrences.note: " The whole house he overlaid with gold ": and therefore every part of
" David " is named, but Solomon, his son, is understood together with him; see
"And all the earth sought the face of Solomon ": i.e., his presence, so as to see him and to speak with him personally
"One tribe" is mentioned; but, by Synecdoche, Simeon and Benjamin are included, as well as the Levites and others who joined the tribe

devices.name: Anthropopatheia
devices.definition: Ascribing to God human feelings, parts, or actions, by way of condescension to us.

devices.name: Hyperbole
devices.definition: Deliberate exaggeration, not meant literally, that drives a point home vividly.

occurrences.note: " There was no more spirit in her ": i.e., she was dazed or stupefied, as we say, with astonishment
Silver and gold as stones
"The boasting of Benhadad."

devices.name: Pleonasm
devices.definition: A deliberate redundancy — more words than strictly needed — to underline or solemnise.

occurrences.note: " Thou... knowest the hearts of all the children of men ": i.e., of all men, with emphasis on the "all." Ecc
" Thou spakest by the hand of Moses thy servant": i.e., by Moses. Jehovah was the speaker, Moses was only the instrument. So also

devices.name: Paroemia (proverb)
devices.definition: A proverb — a wayside-saying in common use, cited or coined.

occurrences.note: "A merciful Ilia n is merciful to his beast."

devices.name: Synonymia
devices.definition: Amassing synonyms — words of like meaning — to enforce and enlarge a point.

devices.name: Gnome (quotation)
devices.definition: A quotation or proverbial maxim woven in — a pithy saying cited for authority or point.

devices.name: Idiom
devices.definition: A peculiar usage of the Hebrew or Greek that does not carry its literal force — an idiom to be rendered by its sense, not word for word.

occurrences.note: Jeroboam "made Israel to sin ": i.e., was the cause of Israel's sin by setting up the two calves in Bethel and Dan

devices.name: Polyonymia
devices.definition: Heaping up several different names or titles for the same person or thing.

devices.name: Polyptoton
devices.definition: Repetition of the same root word in different inflections (“dying you shall die”).

occurrences.note: "The people piped with pipes, and rejoiced with great joy ": i.e., their joy scarcely knew bounds
The heaven and heaven of heavens cannot contain thee ": i.e., the highest heaven." Ecc. i. 2

devices.name: Epitrechon
devices.definition: A clause “running through” — dropped in parenthetically between others.

devices.name: Epizeuxis
devices.definition: Immediate repetition of a word for intense emphasis, with nothing between (“Lord, Lord”).

devices.name: Heterosis
devices.definition: Exchange of one grammatical form for another — of tense, number, person, degree, or mood (e.g. a future used for a command).

occurrences.note: " Go forth, and do so ": i.e., thou mayest go, and do

devices.name: Irony
devices.definition: Saying the opposite of what is meant, so the real sense is felt through the contrast.

occurrences.note: The words of Elijah to the prophets of Baal were sarcasm of the severest kind
The words of the prophet Micaiah to Ahab and Jehoshaphat: " Go, and prosper "; to show by Irony the false prophecies of Ahab's own prophets

devices.name: Paronomasia (wordplay)
devices.definition: A play on words that sound alike but differ in sense — pun, rhyme, near-repetition.

devices.name: Rhetorical question
devices.definition: A question asked for effect, not for an answer — to affirm, deny, or provoke thought.

devices.name: Antimetabole
devices.definition: Words repeated in reverse order and grammatical relation (“sabbath for man … man for sabbath”).

devices.name: Battologia
devices.definition: Vain, mechanical repetition of the same words without added meaning (rebuked, Matt 6:7).

devices.name: Enigma
devices.definition: A dark saying — a truth wrapped in obscure or riddling terms.

devices.name: Epanadiplosis
devices.definition: A clause encircled — beginning and ending with the same word.

devices.name: Epitrope
devices.definition: Admission or permission — ironically conceding a point (“Fill up the measure of your fathers”).

occurrences.note: " Go, and prosper: for the Lord shall deliver it into the hand of the king." Micaiah (by Epitrope and Irony) admitted what was in Jehoshaphat's heart, and thus exposed and condemned it. Ecc

devices.name: Hendiadys
devices.definition: One idea expressed by two words joined with “and,” the second really qualifying the first.

occurrences.note: " Now the men divined and hasted": i.e., divined, yes — and quickly too; or, as in A.V., " diligently observed," with the emphasis on the word diligently

devices.name: Hypallage
devices.definition: Interchange: a word logically belonging to one term is grammatically attached to another.

devices.name: Hysteresis
devices.definition: A later passage supplying a detail not recorded in the earlier narrative it refers to.

devices.name: Parallelism
devices.definition: Successive lines echo one another in structure — saying the same thing twice, or balancing matched clauses.

devices.name: Personification
devices.definition: Giving human traits, action, or speech to something impersonal or abstract.
